question: What is the number of natural numbers less than or equal to 1000 and divisible by 5 or 7?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use inclusion-exclusion

Multiples of 5 = 1000 ÷ 5 = 200

Multiples of 7 = 1000 ÷ 7 = 142

Common (35) = 1000 ÷ 35 = 28

Total = 200 + 142 − 28 = 314

**∴ Answer = 314**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Numbers ≤ 1000 divisible by 5 or 7

**Formula used:**

n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Multiples of 5 = ⌊1000/5⌋ = 200

⇒ Multiples of 7 = ⌊1000/7⌋ = 142

⇒ Multiples of 35 = ⌊1000/35⌋ = 28

⇒ Total = 200 + 142 − 28

⇒ = 314

**∴ The correct answer is 314.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inclusion-Exclusion Principle

n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B)

LCM Concept

Common multiples use LCM (5 × 7 = 35)

Floor Function

⌊n/m⌋ gives count of multiples

Key Idea

Subtract overlap to avoid double counting
